blocks.text: DUMAGUETE CITY, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd), Commission on Higher Education (CHEd) and Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (Tesda) are expanding opportunities for Filipino learners through One Education, a program that aims to strengthen learner support and provide more flexible pathways across education, skills training and employment. During the Fourth Joint Education Trifocal Management Committee (JETMC4) meeting in Dumaguete City, the three agencies highlighted the Learning Initiatives for Nurturing Guidance Associates and Counselors (LINGAP) Program. They also launched the Localized Access Pathways and Institutional Transitions (LAPIT) Index and the Integrated Ladderized Education-to-Employment Pathways (ILEEP).
